pull.title: KAFKA-21276: Stop fetching standby changelogs while records beyond the limit offset are buffered
pull.body:
A standby task whose store uses the input topic as its changelog may
only apply records up to the offset committed by the active task, but
`StoreChangelogReader` kept fetching beyond that offset. Those records
stayed in the restore buffer, which could grow until `OutOfMemoryError`
when the active task was far behind the end of the topic.

This PR pauses such a changelog partition while its buffer holds records
beyond the limit offset, and resumes it once the limit has moved past
them. This is how standby tasks worked before 2.5.0: `StreamThread`
paused the partition when `StandbyTask#update` returned records beyond
the limit, and this was lost in the refactoring of KAFKA-9113 (#7997).
The change adds no new config or public API.

The new test in `OptimizedKTableIntegrationTest` pauses the active task
and produces 1,000 more records: without the fix the standby polls all
of them beyond the committed offset; with the fix it polls once (at most
`max.poll.records`) and pauses the partition.

Related to KAFKA-19992 / KIP-1325.

Reviewers: Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

review_comments.body: The bufferedLimitIndex needs to be kept updated, otherwise the paused standby will be stuck forever, right? If so, we should add a comment to maybeUpdateLimitOffsetsForStandbyChangelogs and a test to guard against a silent hang.

I added a comment there in 91c6095c1f.

For the test, `shouldResumeSourceChangelogStandbyOnceLimitPassesBufferedRecords` already guards against this hang: it fails if the limit update skips paused partitions. I added a comment to the test to make that clear.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21276: Stop fetching standby changelogs while records beyond the limit offset are buffered

A standby task whose store uses the input topic as its changelog may only
apply records up to the offset committed by the active task. The restore
consumer kept fetching beyond that offset, and the records stayed in the
restore buffer, so the buffer could grow until OutOfMemoryError when the
active task was far behind the end of the topic.

Pause a changelog partition while its buffer holds records that cannot be
applied yet, and resume it once the limit has moved past them.
KAFKA-21276: Explain how a paused standby changelog partition is resumed
